description: Pouch, box or roll that holds several pens and pencils; a sleeve for one pen is a Pen sleeve.
Device that drives a wire staple through sheets to join them.
General-purpose scissors for paper and household use.
Hand stamp with a rubber die for dates, words or marks on office papers; decorative stamps are in Craft & Art Supplies.
Inked pad for office stamps; ink pads for decorative stamps are in Craft & Art Supplies.
Personal seal stamped as a signature, used in Japan.
Solid glue in a twist-up tube for sticking paper.
Narrow transparent adhesive tape for paper and desk use.
Two-legged instrument that draws circles and arcs (a navigation compass is in Sports, Fitness & Recreation).
Small scale for weighing letters and parcels for postage.
Frame of beads on rods moved by hand to calculate; the Japanese soroban is one form.
Pair of sliding logarithmic scales for multiplying and dividing.
Machine that cuts paper into strips or particles.
Device that prints adhesive labels on tape; it may stand alone or connect to a computer or phone.
Machine that prints characters on paper as keys are struck, manual or electric.
Bottled ink made for fountain pens; sold by dye or pigment, wetness, saturation, shading, sheen, water resistance and colour.
Tube of leads made for mechanical pencils, in different grades and diameters.
Sleeve or case that holds one pen.
Tabs made to fit one planner system.
Tape cartridge made to fit one label-maker system.
Pen that feeds liquid ink from a reservoir to a split nib; filling system, nib size and shape, and body material vary.
Holder with loose nibs dipped in a separate bottle of ink; a dip pen sold for comics or drawing only is in Craft & Art Supplies.
Pen that rolls thick oil-based ink onto paper through a ball tip; a digital pen that writes in ink and records the writing is included.
Ball-tip pen with liquid water-based ink; a digital pen of this type that records the writing is included.
Pen with a flexible brush tip sold for handwriting, lettering or calligraphy (fudepens included); brush pens for drawing only are in Craft & Art Supplies.
Brush, ink and inkstone sold as one kit.
Device that sharpens a wooden pencil, manual or electric.
Bound book of blank, lined, dot or graph sheets for notes; also called a journal.
Cover plus refill books sold together as one system (the TRAVELER'S notebook is one); covers and refills sold separately are under Planner covers & refills.
Bound book ruled by date or for dates (daily, weekly, monthly), dated or undated; the Hobonichi Techo is an example.
Printed sheets of the days, weeks or months of a year, for the wall, desk or pocket.
Tear-off or sticky-note day calendar, one sheet per day.
Plain cut sheets sold by the ream for copiers and printers; photographic paper is in Cameras & Photography.
Folded paper cover for posting a letter or document.
Envelope lined with bubble or paper padding for posting small items.
Rigid tube for posting rolled documents.
Sheet of printed self-adhesive stickers sold as stationery (a collectible sticker series is in Coins, Stamps, Medals & Trading Cards).
Cut card of plain or ruled stock sold in packs for notes, filing and revision; when blank it is also a flash card.
Card or plastic cover, folded, pocketed or flapped, that holds loose unpunched sheets without rings or clips.
Pair of plastic films joined at one edge, made to be sealed round a sheet in a laminator; sold in different sizes and thicknesses.
Plastic comb, wire or slide spine made to bind punched sheets in a binding machine; sold in different diameters.
